stem: A solid-organ transplant recipient develops listeriosis several weeks after transplantation. Which exposure route aligns with standard infection references?

options.text: Airborne transmission only across hospital ventilation systems
Listeria occurs only from blood transfusion and never from food
Listeria is transmitted exclusively through donor organ implantation

explanation.rationale_correct: Listeria monocytogenes listeriosis is transmitted by ingestion of contaminated food and may cause CNS infection with high mortality in solid-organ transplant recipients.

rationale_incorrect.B: Listeria transmission is described as foodborne ingestion rather than primarily airborne hospital spread.
rationale_incorrect.C: Contaminated food is the cited mode of transmission rather than transfusion alone.
rationale_incorrect.D: Foodborne acquisition is the described route rather than exclusive donor-organ transmission.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: Mode of transmission: ingestion of contaminated food

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 5 → Listeriosis → C.5. (foodborne transmission); PDF p. 213 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Listeria transmission angle paired with education combo (cctc-1101); distinct from unpasteurized-dairy teaching (cctc-1051); anchor verified on Cupples p. 213.

stem: When evaluating a transplant recipient with suspected Nocardia infection, which anatomic site is most commonly affected per standard references?

options.text: Lung with pneumonitis, pulmonary nodules, or pulmonary abscesses
Isolated nail-bed infection without any pulmonary involvement
Nocardia affects only the gastrointestinal tract in every case
Nocardia is limited to urinary tract infections exclusively

explanation.rationale_correct: Nocardia asteroides is the most common species and the lung is the most common site, presenting as pneumonitis, pulmonary nodules, or pulmonary abscesses; extrapulmonary brain, skin, and bone involvement may also occur.

rationale_incorrect.B: Pulmonary involvement is the most common presentation rather than isolated nail-bed infection.
rationale_incorrect.C: Nocardia most commonly involves the lung rather than exclusively the GI tract.
rationale_incorrect.D: UTI is not described as the exclusive or most common Nocardia site.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: Most common species is Nocardia asteroides … Most common site: lung (pneumonitis, pulmonary nodules, pulmonary abscesses)

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 5 → Nocardiosis → D.1.–3. (pulmonary presentation most common); PDF p. 213 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Nocardia pulmonary-presentation angle paired with listeria/nocardia combo (cctc-1101); anchor verified on Cupples p. 213.

stem: A lung transplant recipient develops community-acquired respiratory virus lower tract infection. Which clinical concern aligns with standard references?

options.text: Lower respiratory CARV infection may be associated with significant morbidity and mortality
Community respiratory viruses never cause lower tract disease in transplant recipients
CARV infections are benign and never require monitoring after transplant
Only bacterial pathogens cause lower respiratory morbidity in solid-organ recipients

explanation.rationale_correct: Community-acquired respiratory viruses are a frequent cause of disease in solid-organ transplant recipients, and lower respiratory tract infection with CARV can be associated with significant morbidity and mortality.

rationale_incorrect.B: CARV may involve the lower respiratory tract with serious outcomes in immunosuppressed recipients.
rationale_incorrect.C: CARV infections warrant monitoring because they may cause significant morbidity and mortality.
rationale_incorrect.D: Viral CARV lower respiratory infections are specifically highlighted as clinically significant.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: Frequent cause of disease in SOT recipients … Lower respiratory tract infection with CARV can be associated with significant morbidity and mortality

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 5 → CARV → K.1.a.–b. (lower respiratory CARV morbidity/mortality); PDF p. 209 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. CARV lower-respiratory severity angle distinct from RSV transmission teaching (cctc-1093) and parainfluenza shedding (cctc-2091); anchor verified on Cupples p. 209.

stem: A coordinator is reviewing influenza and community respiratory virus teaching after transplantation. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Influenza virus infections may range from mild self-limiting illness to serious secondary bacterial infections.
Community-acquired respiratory viruses are a frequent cause of disease in solid-organ transplant recipients.
Influenza never causes secondary bacterial infections in transplant recipients.
Community respiratory viruses cannot involve the lower respiratory tract.

explanation.rationale_correct: Influenza may range from mild illness to serious secondary bacterial infections, and CARV are a frequent cause of disease in solid-organ recipients including lower tract involvement. Statements III and IV are false.

rationale_incorrect.B: Statement IV is false because lower respiratory CARV infection may be serious.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statements I and II are true; statements III and IV are false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statements III and IV are false.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 5, Infectious Diseases → Influenza / CARV → 7.a. and K.1.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Influenza viruses … range from mild, self-limiting syndromes to serious secondary infections … Frequent cause of disease in SOT recipients

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 5 → Influenza → 7.a. (influenza infections range from mild, self-limiting syndromes to serious secondary infections); PDF p. 210 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Influenza/CARV analysis combo distinct from inactivated influenza vaccination teaching (cctc-1048); anchor verified on Cupples p. 210.
